result:
I found one real bug in `eml_parser.parser`: turning on `ignore_bad_start=True` breaks every e-mail it parses. The other two properties I tested passed.

## The bug (High severity, Logic)

**Target:** `EmlParser.decode_email_bytes`, at `eml_parser/parser.py:224-241`.

```python
p = EmlParser()
raw = b"garbage line\nFrom: alice@example.com\nTo: bob@example.org\nSubject: hello\n\nbody\n"
r = p.decode_email_bytes(raw, ignore_bad_start=True)
# r["header"]["to"] == [], r["header"]["subject"] == '', header == {'from': ['alice@example.comTo, <>']}
```

Without the option, the same e-mail gives `['bob@example.org']` and `'hello'`. There are two causes:
1. **Wrong check:** `b':' not in eml_file.split(b'\n', 1)` asks whether a list item equals `b':'`, not whether the first line contains a colon. So the stripping branch runs for almost every input, including valid e-mails.
2. **Newlines dropped:** inside that branch, `_eml_file += line` adds the kept lines back without their `\n`. All headers and the body end up on one line, so recipients, subject, date and body are lost without any error.

This breaks valid e-mails and also the case the option is meant for (junk lines before the headers). The report includes a fix that keeps everything from the first line containing a colon and joins the lines with `\n`. I checked that logic separately on both example e-mails and it parses them correctly. I didn't apply it to the library code.

## Tests that passed
- **`string_sliding_window_loop` covers the whole body:** across 1,000 examples with varied slice sizes and bodies full of `://`, spaces and `>`, every character landed in at least one slice.
- **`decode_email_bytes` doesn't crash:** 500 generated e-mails with random headers (including Date, Received and Content-*), Unicode values and binary bodies all parsed, and the date always came back as a `datetime`.

Files are in `runs/eml-parser_r3/`:
- `bug_report_eml_parser_parser_2026-10-06_01-10_vyaa.md`
- `tests/test_parser.py`
- `tests/repro_ignore_bad_start.py`
